name: Vercel
tagline: Deploy frontend apps, serverless functions, and previews.
shortDescription: A deployment platform with strong Git, CLI, preview, environment, and framework workflows.
agentSummary: Agents can deploy previews, inspect builds, manage projects, read deployment logs, search docs, and connect through Vercel's hosted MCP server.
bestFor: Next.js deployment, preview URLs, build diagnostics, and production releases.
cautionNotes: Key limitations: Environment variable and production deploy permissions need tight control. Deploys, secret changes, IAM, billing, networking, deletes, and rollback paths have high production blast radius; require scoped credentials and review gates. MCP servers inherit the connected account's scopes and may send prompts or data to third-party services; configure read-only or narrow scopes when available. CLI access is powerful but can run destructive local or production commands; prefer dry runs, preview environments, and non-production credentials.
pricingSummary: Public pricing with free, Pro, Enterprise, bandwidth, and function usage dimensions.
authModel: CLI login, tokens, team scopes, Git provider auth, and OAuth for the hosted Vercel MCP server.
accountCreation: Self-serve signup via Git providers or email.
browserSupport: Dashboard is important for project settings, logs, and billing.

capabilities.detail: CLI supports deploys, builds, env, logs, projects, and domains.
Vercel's official remote MCP server searches docs, manages projects and deployments, and analyzes deployment logs.
Official docs are listed for API behavior, authentication, limits, examples, and setup review.
Public pricing with free, Pro, Enterprise, bandwidth, and function usage dimensions.
Self-serve signup via Git providers or email.
Dashboard helps inspect builds, analytics, and configuration.
The tool has documented test, local, preview, self-hosted, or staging paths that let agents validate changes away from production.
REST API supports deployment and project automation.
